message:
fix(update): follow the ownership chain, not just the first link

Product 1, test 2, build 0. Kept as its own commit: it fixes an updater defect that predates
the preview work and would be worth having on its own.

Ownership stopped at the immediate parent and required THAT parent to own a window. A product
two tiers deep fits; ours is three. GNLinkHost owns a window and starts GNLinkStream, which owns
none and starts GNLinkCapture, which owns none either -- so the third tier could not be
recognised as anybody's child. It was not an orphan either, because its parent is alive, so it
fell through to a direct request, and a windowless process cannot be asked. PrepareForSwap then
abandons the update before touching the disk.

The trigger, stated exactly rather than as "GDI mode breaks updates": an update is abandoned
when a process in the stop list is windowless AND its parent is also in the list, also
windowless, and still alive. For the product that is GNLinkCapture with GNLinkStream above it,
which is the arrangement whenever the host has fallen back to GDI capture. It is reproduced
here with a fixture, in the field's own words -- reverting this walk makes the three-tier case
fail with "could not ask pid N to stop", the same sentence the 09-11 log recorded. It has NOT
been executed against the shipped product; no installed process was touched.

What the walk does not relax. Every edge still needs a real parentPid match, a known creation
time on both ends, and a parent older than the process it owns. The search only ever looks
inside preparedTargets_, so a parent outside the stop list still ends it. A depth cap and a
visited set mean termination does not depend on the process table being well formed. Ownership
is still only granted on reaching a target that owns a window -- "windowless with a parent" is
not ownership, and a chain that runs out returns the same nullptr it always did.

Eight synthetic cases and a real three-tier process tree. The synthetic ones ask one question
throughout -- was this pid asked directly -- because PrepareForSwap only asks what it has not
left to a supervisor: three tiers, enumeration order reversed, the two-tier shape unchanged, a
live parent outside the list, a chain that never reaches a window, a parent younger than its
child, an unknown creation time mid-chain, and a cycle. The real fixture is a windowed root
starting a windowless middle starting a windowless leaf, with the production enumerator
reporting the shape, because the synthetic cases describe parentage and this one produces it.

A leftover child still stops the update, and now does so by the owned-child path: the leaf is
held on an event the branch does not release, Quiesce refuses, and it names it as a child that
outlived its parent. Nothing is force-terminated and the swap does not happen.

236 checks in update_effects_test and 43 in update_stop_process_test, the latter three runs
clean. Reverting the walk breaks 3 of the synthetic set and 7 of the real one, and nothing else
in either -- the blast radius is the three-tier case and only that.

The first version of the leftover-child case was wrong and passed for the wrong reason: it put
the leaf on the root's own quit event, which the root signals when it closes, so the leaf was
released along with everything else and there was nothing for Quiesce to object to.
